related_questions.question: What is the difference between IRC 105 and 106?
related_questions.snippet: Generally, IRC Section 106(a) excludes employer-provided coverage under an accident or health plan from employees' income. Under IRC Section 105(b), employees may exclude amounts received through employer-provided accident or health insurance if the reimbursement is for medical care incurred by the participant.

text_blocks.snippet: IRC Section 106, specifically §106(a), generally excludes employer-provided coverage under an accident or health plan from an employee's gross income. This means that if an employer pays for health insurance premiums or contributes to a health plan for their employees, those contributions are not considered taxable income for the employee.

list.title: Exclusion of Employer Contributions:
list.snippet: The core of §106 is that employer contributions to accident and health plans are excluded from an employee's gross income.

list.title: Applies to Various Plans:
list.snippet: This exclusion applies to various types of employer-sponsored health plans, including those that provide coverage for employees, their spouses, and dependents.

list.title: Section 105 Relationship:
list.snippet: Section 106 often works in conjunction with §105, which addresses the tax treatment of amounts received under accident and health plans. Specifically, §105(b) addresses the exclusion of amounts received by an employee for medical care expenses.

list.title: Specific Provisions:
list.snippet: While §106(a) is the general rule, other subsections address specific types of plans, such as those involving Archer MSAs (§106(b)), long-term care benefits through flexible spending arrangements (§106(c)), and health savings accounts (§106(d)).

list.title: No Inference for Cafeteria Plans:
list.snippet: It's important to note that §106 does not extend to situations where employees have a choice between employer contributions to a health plan and other taxable or nontaxable benefits, such as under a cafeteria plan.

list.title: Rev. Rul. 82-196:
list.snippet: This ruling clarifies that employer contributions to accident and health plans covering retirees and their beneficiaries are also excludable under §106.

list.title: Rev. Rul. 67-360:
list.snippet: This ruling clarifies that employer contributions to a health plan trust fund are also excludable under §106.

list.title: Decedent's Estates:
list.snippet: Employer contributions to a health plan for a deceased employee's surviving spouse and dependents are also excludable under §106, with the taxation of payments made to the survivors determined under §105, according to the IRS.
